title: Scout Badges
description1: The Scout badge system is a support for leaders and scouts to plan and implement the Scout program in a way that helps scouts grow as people. The badges make it easier to connect knowledge, experiences and goals in scouting activities.
description2: After a completed project, a semester, or when the scouts have learned something new, a badge serves as a memory of what you have done together.
description3: A badge is therefore much more than just a piece of cloth. It becomes proof of what you have learned, what you have tried, and what adventures you have had together with your patrol or department.
badgePlacement: There are designated places on the scout uniform for different types of badges. Participation-, qualification-, proof- and interest badges are placed on the left sleeve, while patrol badges and age group badges are sewn onto the right breast pocket. The Swedish, European and world organization badges are located at the top of the right sleeve.
badgeTypes: As a sea scout, there are also special badges that belong to sea and water activities. They show affiliation, interest and sometimes also what knowledge or skills you have trained in the activity.
badgeVariants: There are many different badges in Scouting, such as membership badges, participation badges, qualification badges, proof badges and interest badges. Each category has its own meaning, and together they show both what you belong to and what you have developed during your time in Scouting.
